title: Rheumatic heart disease and mitral valve disease

steps.tx: The Revised **Jones Criteria** govern the clinical diagnosis of **acute rheumatic fever** following group A streptococcal pharyngitis. Confirmation mandates microbiologic or serologic proof of preceding streptococcal infection along with either two major manifestations or one major criterion plus two minor criteria.

steps.tx: Hemodynamically, severe rheumatic mitral stenosis is characterised by a restricted anatomical **mitral valve area** of 1.5 cm2 or less, with critical or very severe stenosis exhibiting an area of 1.0 cm2 or less. Doppler assessment reveals a prolonged transmitral **pressure half-time** exceeding 150 ms, reaching 220 ms or greater in very severe obstruction.

steps.tx: Panel A shows thickened domed anterior leaflet motion with the classic hockey stick shape plus a severely enlarged left atrium, the structural face of chronic rheumatic obstruction. Panel B quantifies it with a **mitral valve area** of 1.0 square cm and a **pressure half time** of 220 ms with a raised mean gradient. Meeting these **very severe thresholds** matters because tighter stenosis predicts pulmonary hypertension and favours timely commissurotomy referral.
steps.say: On the left, the mitral leaflets look thick and dome open like a hockey stick, and the left atrium is hugely enlarged from years of obstruction. On the right, Doppler measurement gives a valve area of 1.0 square cm with a pressure half time of 220 milliseconds and a high mean gradient. Those values meet very severe disease cutoffs, which is why this combination of shape plus numbers should prompt assessment for balloon commissurotomy.

vis.alt: Two panel echo shows domed thickened mitral leaflets with left atrial enlargement and Doppler measurements of severe stenosis.

steps.tx: The multi-component **Wilkins echocardiographic score** grades mitral valve morphology to determine anatomical suitability for **percutaneous mitral balloon commissurotomy**. The score evaluates leaflet mobility, subvalvular thickening, leaflet thickening, and calcification from 1 to 4 each, reaching a maximum of 16 points. A score of 8 or less predicts excellent procedural outcomes without significant leaflet tearing.

steps.tx: Clear procedural **Contraindications to PMBC** must be ruled out by transesophageal echocardiography prior to balloon dilation. Essential absolute contraindications include documented **left atrial thrombus**, moderate-to-severe mitral regurgitation greater than grade 2+, severe bicommissural calcification, or concomitant severe aortic valve disease requiring surgical valve replacement.

steps.tx: **Primary mitral regurgitation** is caused by intrinsic structural defects of the leaflets, chordae, or annulus. Degenerative severe MR is defined on quantitative Doppler echocardiography by an effective regurgitant orifice area of 0.40 cm2 or greater and a calculated total **regurgitant volume** of 60 mL or greater per beat.

steps.tx: In asymptomatic severe primary MR, early surgical repair prevents irreversible left ventricular decompensation. The primary Class I **surgical indication** in asymptomatic patients requires evidence of incipient LV systolic dysfunction, defined as an LVEF of 60% or lower, or progressive chamber dilation reflected by an **LVESD** of 40 mm or greater.

nodes.label: Echo triggers: LVEF <= 60% or LVESD >= 40 mm
Secondary triggers: new AF or PASP > 50 mmHg
Mitral valve repair by experienced team

steps.tx: **Secondary mitral regurgitation** develops when ischemic or non-ischemic LV remodeling displaces the papillary muscles, causing abnormal **leaflet tethering** across an anatomically intact valve. Because secondary MR imposes volume overload onto an already failing ventricle, severe secondary MR is defined by lower quantitative thresholds, specifically an EROA of 0.20 cm2 or greater and regurgitant volume of 30 mL or greater.

points: Initial treatment is guideline HF therapy

steps.tx: For patients with persistent severe secondary MR despite optimal guideline-directed medical therapy, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair utilizing the **MitraClip** system improves survival and cuts HF hospitalisations. Benefit was established in the **COAPT trial**, which required an LVEF between 20% and 50%, an LVESD of 70 mm or less, and persistent NYHA II to IV symptoms.
